# IPA Sound Drill

> Drill your English sounds with IPA. A free, open, browser-based tool for learning English pronunciation using the International Phonetic Alphabet.

IPA Sound Drill helps learners understand sound-to-spelling relationships and rebuild their pronunciation from the sound level. Built on the principle "you can't hear what you can't say," the app is designed for non-native English speakers who want to systematically improve their pronunciation using IPA notation. Both General American (GA) and Received Pronunciation (RP) are supported for every word and phrase.

## Modes

- **Decode**: See IPA notation (e.g., /kætəˌpɪlər/), type the English word (caterpillar)
- **Encode**: See the English word, transcribe to IPA using an on-screen IPA keyboard
- **Sound → Vocabulary (Mode B)**: Listen to audio and identify the correct word from context, then check meaning and IPA
- **Connected Speech**: Practice linking, weak forms (36 function words), and 201 phrase-level pronunciation patterns
- **Vocabulary Browser**: Search 5,397 CEFR-graded words with GA/RP IPA, respelling, and audio

## Languages

Interface available in 6 languages:

- English (`/en/`)
- Japanese (`/ja/`)
- Korean (`/ko/`)
- Simplified Chinese (`/zh-Hans/`)
- Traditional Chinese (`/zh-Hant/`)
- Filipino (`/fil/`)

## Data

- Wordlist: 5,397 CEFR-graded English words with both General American (GA) and Received Pronunciation (RP) IPA
- Connected speech phrases: 201 (with CEFR badges)
- Weak forms: 36 function words with weak/strong IPA and GA/RP variants
- Phoneme inventory: 44 English phonemes plus stress marks and allophones (flap, glottal stop, syllabic consonants)
- Multilingual phoneme explanations: 6 languages

## Technology

Static HTML + vanilla JS + JSON data + Google Apps Script (TTS proxy). Hosted on Vercel. No sign-up. No ads. Cookieless analytics only (Vercel Web Analytics).

## Phonemes covered

### Vowels — monophthongs (GA)

- `i` — long ee (see /si/)
- `ɪ` — short i (sit /sɪt/)
- `ɛ` — eh (bed /bɛd/)
- `æ` — a~eh (cat /kæt/)
- `ə` — schwa (about /əˈbaʊt/)
- `ʌ` — uh (cup /kʌp/)
- `ɑ` — ah (hot /hɑt/, father)
- `ɔ` — aw (dog /dɔɡ/, thought)
- `ʊ` — short u (book /bʊk/)
- `u` — long oo (food /fud/)
- `ɝ` — stressed er (bird /bɝd/) — GA rhotic
- `ɚ` — unstressed er (water /ˈwɔtɚ/) — GA rhotic

### Vowels — diphthongs

- `eɪ` — ay (day /deɪ/)
- `aɪ` — eye (my /maɪ/)
- `ɔɪ` — oy (boy /bɔɪ/)
- `oʊ` — oh (go /ɡoʊ/)
- `aʊ` — ow (now /naʊ/)

### Consonants — fricatives / affricates

- `θ` — voiceless th (think /θɪŋk/)
- `ð` — voiced th (this /ðɪs/)
- `ʃ` — sh (she /ʃi/)
- `ʒ` — zh (measure /ˈmɛʒɚ/)
- `tʃ` — ch (church /tʃɝtʃ/)
- `dʒ` — j (judge /dʒʌdʒ/)
- `f` — f (fan)
- `v` — v (van)
- `s` — s (see)
- `z` — z (zoo)
- `h` — h (hat)

### Consonants — stops / nasals / approximants

- `p b t d k ɡ` — plosives
- `m n ŋ` — nasals (sing /sɪŋ/ for ŋ)
- `r l w j` — approximants
- `ɾ` — flap / tap (butter /ˈbʌɾɚ/ in GA)
- `ʔ` — glottal stop (button /ˈbʌʔn̩/)
- `n̩` `l̩` — syllabic consonants (button, bottle)

### Stress marks

- `ˈ` — primary stress on the next syllable
- `ˌ` — secondary stress

## GA vs RP — key differences the app teaches

- **Rhoticity**: GA pronounces `r` after vowels (car /kɑr/); RP typically drops it (car /kɑː/).
- **er sound**: GA uses `ɝ`/`ɚ`; RP uses `ɜː`/`ə`.
- **The LOT/CLOTH vowel**: GA `ɑ` or `ɔ` where RP uses `ɒ` (hot GA /hɑt/ vs RP /hɒt/).
- **Bath vowel**: GA `æ` where RP uses `ɑː` (bath GA /bæθ/ vs RP /bɑːθ/).
- **Flap t**: GA turns intervocalic `t` into `ɾ` (water /ˈwɔɾɚ/); RP keeps `t`.

Every word and phrase in the app shows both GA and RP IPA side-by-side.

## Sample weak forms (all 36 in-app)

Function words reduce to weak forms in unstressed positions. Learning weak forms is the single fastest way to sound natural.

- **a** — weak /ə/ before a consonant (strong /ə/)
- **an** — weak /ən/ before a vowel (strong /æn/)
- **the** — weak /ðə/ before a consonant (strong /ðə/, /ði/ before a vowel)
- **to** — weak /tə/ before a consonant (strong /tu/)
- **of** — weak /əv/, often /ə/ before a consonant (strong /ʌv/)
- **and** — weak /ən/ with d dropped (strong /ænd/)
- **for** — weak /fɚ/ GA / /fə/ RP (strong /fɔr/)
- **from** — weak /frəm/ (strong /frʌm/)
- **at** — weak /ət/ (strong /æt/)
- **than** — weak /ðən/ (strong /ðæn/)
- **was** — weak /wəz/ (strong /wɑz/)
- **were** — weak /wɚ/ GA / /wə/ RP (strong /wɝ/)
- **can** — weak /kən/ (strong /kæn/ when stressed)
- **have / has / had** — weak /həv/ /həz/ /həd/ (often reduced to /əv/ /əz/ /əd/ after a pronoun)
- **your** — weak /jɚ/ GA / /jə/ RP (strong /jɔr/)
- **them** — weak /ðəm/, often /əm/ casually
- **he / him / his / her** — h-drop mid-sentence: /i/ /ɪm/ /ɪz/ /ɚ/

## Sample connected speech patterns (from the 201 in-app phrases)

### Linking (consonant → vowel)

- **an apple** — /əˈnæpəl/ — n links onto the next vowel: "a-napple"
- **pick it up** — /ˈpɪkɪˈtʌp/ — k→it, t→up link consonants to vowels
- **come on** — /kʌˈmɑn/ — m links into on: "co-mon"
- **look at** — /ˈlʊkət/ — k links into at: "loo-kat"
- **turn off** — /tɝˈnɔf/ — n links into off: "tur-noff"

### Glide insertion

- **I am** — /aɪˈjæm/ — a /j/ glide bridges I→am
- **go away** — /ˌɡoʊwəˈweɪ/ — a /w/ glide bridges go→away
- **the end** — /ðiˈjɛnd/ — the→/ði/ before a vowel, /j/ glide

### Assimilation (yod-coalescence)

- **did you** — /ˈdɪdʒu/ — d + y → /dʒ/
- **would you** — /ˈwʊdʒu/ — d + y → /dʒ/
- **don't you** — /ˈdoʊntʃu/ — t + y → /tʃ/

## Who this is for

- Non-native English learners (CEFR A1–C2) who want to fix pronunciation at the sound level, not the word level
- Learners preparing for IELTS / TOEFL / TOEIC speaking sections where connected speech and weak forms distinguish upper bands
- ESL / EFL teachers who need a free, no-signup tool for classroom demos of IPA, GA vs RP, weak forms, and connected speech
- Self-studiers who already know some IPA and want structured drill on the 44 English phonemes
- Interface languages: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Filipino

## Why free and open

- **No ads.** No display ads, no affiliate content, no upsell.
- **No sign-up.** No account required, no email collected, no login.
- **No tracking beyond privacy-preserving analytics.** Uses Vercel Web Analytics (cookieless, no personal data). No third-party trackers.
- **Open source.** Full code and data on GitHub: https://github.com/nkhippo/IPASoundDrill
- **Built for learners, not for engagement metrics.** No streaks, no gamification pressure. Practice as long or short as helps.
